title: Broken Relationships from Sin
definition: The doctrine of Broken Relationships from Sin teaches that sin fractures relationships through blame, selfishness, bitterness, abuse of power, fear, and refusal to love as God commands.
summary: Broken Relationships from Sin names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. sin fractures relationships through blame, selfishness, bitterness, abuse of power, fear, and refusal to love as God commands. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Broken Relationships from Sin because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: sin fractures relationships through blame, selfishness, bitterness, abuse of power, fear, and refusal to love as God commands. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because relational pain is often treated only as personality conflict when Scripture also exposes sin and calls for healing truth. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Seek peace without pretending wrong is harmless. Repent where you have sinned, forgive as Christ enables, and pursue wise help where harm has been done. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
